title: Route/Model/Customer Cost & Latency Signature Generator
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Build a backend service that computes compact cost and latency 'signatures' for every inference request and emits per-route, per-model, and per-customer breakdowns suitable for Console dashboards, chargeback reports, and alerting. The service must reconcile token-level cost, model variant routing, KV cache delta, and observed latency across streaming and non-streaming responses. Outputs are intended for both near-real-time dashboards (1m/5m windows) and daily rollups for billing reconciliation.

Scope and constraints:
- Input sources: request metadata from ingestion Kafka topic (ingest.requests.v2), runtime telemetry (runtime.metrics.v3), token-usage events (tokens.emitted), and model routing decisions (router.events).
- Compute granularity: single-request signature composed of cost_components (model_compute, cached_kv_savings, batching_adjustment, io_cost) and latency_components (queue_ms, model_compute_ms, network_ms, client_streaming_ms).
- Outputs: 1) streaming per-request signatures to analytics.topic.econ_signatures for downstream consumers; 2) aggregated per-route/per-model/per-customer hourly and daily rollups in ClickHouse and backup in BigQuery for billing audits.
- Multi-tenancy: keep tenant isolation in computation and storage; ensure no cross-tenant leakage. Use customer IDs and anonymize session IDs where needed.
- Performance: per-request processing latency target <= 200ms median for non-batched writes; 95th < 500ms. Backpressure when downstream ClickHouse is congested must preserve core runtime SLA by buffering and dropping low-priority debug fields.
- Accuracy: cost attribution should match finance's token pricing table within a 0.5% error for sample workloads, accounting for quantization and rounding rules.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Attribution algorithm: start with token-level cost mapping using model-specific per-token unit_cost + per-inference fixed overhead amortized by batch size. Apply KV cache savings by comparing request.prefix_kv_hits and prefix_length to expected cache hit model. For routing fallbacks, attach fallback_reason and include both primary and fallback model cost lines where applicable.
- Latency breakdown: use synchronized timestamps from ingest and runtime traces. For streaming responses, compute streaming tail latency (time from first token to final token) and include per-chunk compute times when available. When timestamps disagree, prefer runtime.metrics timestamps and flag requests for later diagnosis.
- Data join strategy: implement a windowed join between ingestion events and telemetry using request_id as the primary key. Use a 60s join window with tombstone handling for late arrivals. Late events beyond 24h should be written to a late-arrivals topic and processed in a daily correction job rather than blocking the real-time pipeline.
- Aggregation: use event-time tumbling windows for hourly/daily, with incremental materialized views to support Console queries. Store both raw signature snapshots and reduced rollups (p50/p95/p99 for latency components and sum/mean for cost components).
- Storage schema: flattened signature JSON for per-request topic; in ClickHouse, use a denormalized table with columns for route_id, model_id, customer_id, cost_components_json, latency_components_json, created_at. Keep an ingest_id and row_version for reconciliation.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end pipeline that produces per-request signature messages for 99% of traffic in production region us-west-2 for a selected beta customer set.
- Console dashboard widgets can display p50/p95 latency component breakdown and per-route cost share for the last 30 days with <= 30s refresh for recent windows.
- A daily job produces a billing reconciliation CSV for finance that reconciles with raw token billing within 0.5% for test dataset.
- Automated tests covering join correctness, fallback attribution, and late-arrival correction logic.

Observability and debugging:
- Emit structured tracing spans for join and attribution steps. Tag spans with join_lag_ms and reason for missing telemetry.
- Expose metrics: signatures_emitted_total, signature_processing_latency_ms_bucket, late_events_dropped_total, percent_with_full_telemetry.
- Create a Console-runbook with steps to reprocess a window, find missing telemetry, and how to force a resync from Kafka to ClickHouse.

Privacy and compliance:
- PII: do not store user-visible prompts or client payloads in signatures; store only hashed session_id and route_id.
- For customers using Private deployments, provide an opt-out mode that routes signatures to customer-owned ClickHouse rather than Redwood-managed topics.
implementation_plan:
Milestones:
1) Prototype (2 weeks): stream-per-request signatures from a shim connector that joins sample runtime traces to ingestion events; smoke-test with beta routes.
2) Core service (3 weeks): implement stateful windowed join, attribution logic, and streaming exporter to analytics.topic.econ_signatures. Add unit and integration tests.
3) Aggregation (2 weeks): ClickHouse schema, hourly rollups, and Console API endpoints.
4) Hardening (2 weeks): backpressure handling, late-arrival correction job, reconciliation job for finance.
5) Beta rollout (1 week): enable for 5 customers, gather feedback, and tune heuristics.
6) GA (1 week): documentation, runbook, and enablement.

Initial owners: Diego (service lead), Aisha (backend instrumentation), Priya (analytics/ClickHouse schema).
comments: 2026-02-16 - Diego Morales: Kickoff meeting held. Agreed on primary data sources and join key. Assigned prototype spike to Aisha. Action: draft Confluence design doc.

2026-02-23 - Aisha Kumar: Prototype emits signatures for 80% of sampled requests; missing telemetry mostly due to router.events being delayed. Added a 60s join window and a side-topic for late arrivals. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4124

2026-03-01 - Engineering review: Feedback from Marco (infra) to add circuit-breaker when ClickHouse queue grows > 1M pending rows. Also noted need for a compact binary schema for per-request messages to reduce network I/O.

2026-03-04 - QA: Found edge case where streaming responses with interleaved partials had negative compute_ms after naive subtraction. Fixed by bounding component durations and added test vectors. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4198
2026-03-08 - Diego Morales: Integration tests green on staging for beta tenants. Begin behind-flag rollout to 5 customers in us-west-2. Observed signature_processing_latency_ms median ~140ms.

2026-03-10 - Priya Shah: Schema for ClickHouse submitted. Dashboard prototype shows per-route cost share but needs normalization by daily requests. Created dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/econ-signature-beta
notes: This ticket focuses on the canonical per-request signature and streaming outputs. Separate follow-ups will implement advanced sampling, ML-based attribution heuristics, and downstream chargeback export formats.
